prompt:
Implement the release-train planner throughout this repository, retaining the exported API and standard-library-only Go 1.23 module. This is a graph, fixed-point planning, atomic editing, and transport integration change, not a new parallel implementation. The 48 catalog manifests are one interconnected workspace; preserve the existing public tests and entrypoints. Add focused regression tests.

GRAPH AND VALIDATION. Build owns a deep copy of its input. Package names and nonempty group names match [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*; all three version components are in [0,1000000000]. Every dependency names an existing different package, appears at most once per owner (even with different kinds), has kind runtime/build/dev and policy pin/compatible/any. Detect cycles using runtime and build edges only; dev edges may form cycles. Members of a nonempty lockstep group must have identical initial versions. Build returns *ValidationError wrapping ErrInvalid, with the following deterministic precedence and Code/Names: package (all invalid package names, versions or group names, listing their package names), duplicate (all duplicated names), dependency (all owners with any invalid dependency), cycle (ALL vertices belonging to any cyclic strongly connected component, excluding acyclic ancestors/descendants), group (all members of the lexicographically first mismatching group). Names is sorted and deduplicated. Empty graphs are valid. Packages() is lexicographically name-sorted and returns fresh slices, including dependency slices.

PLANNING. Rank accepts exactly none/patch/minor/major as 0/1/2/3; otherwise -1. Validate every change, including none, against graph membership and levels; invalid requests return ErrInvalid and a zero Plan. Duplicate seeds combine by maximum rank. Nonzero seeds gain reason direct. Compute the LEAST fixed point: runtime pin propagates any nonzero upstream bump as patch; runtime compatible propagates only upstream major as minor; runtime any never propagates; build propagates any nonzero upstream bump as patch regardless of policy; dev never propagates. Whenever an edge's final source rank activates this rule, the target gains dependency:<source>, even when its own rank was already greater. Each group with at least two members raises all member ranks to the group's maximum, repeatedly with dependency propagation until stable; when that maximum is positive, EVERY group member gains group:<group>, including the original seed. Singleton groups add no group reason. Private nodes participate fully in validation, propagation and groups; IncludePrivate controls only output visibility. Produce one Release per visible nonzero rank in name order. Apply only the maximum bump to the original version: patch increments patch; minor increments minor and clears patch; major increments major and clears minor/patch. Any final version exceeding the component limit, including on hidden private nodes, fails with ErrInvalid/zero Plan. Reasons are unique and lexicographically sorted. Before is the original version, Level the final bump. Releases and Waves must be nonnil empty slices when empty; Graph.Plan revision is zero. Never mutate inputs or retain returned result slices.

SCHEDULING AND IDENTITY. Waves are parallel Kahn layers over VISIBLE released packages only, with runtime/build dependency edges between those visible releases; omit dev, unchanged and hidden-private vertices/edges rather than inventing transitive edges. Each entire ready set is a sorted wave, dependency waves first. Fingerprint is lowercase SHA256 hex over the concatenation of name-sorted releases, each encoded exactly as name=MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH:reason1,reason2\n (After version; literal newline). An empty plan hashes the empty string. WriteReport emits each wave as 'wave N: name1,name2\n', numbering from 1, then each release as 'NAME A.B.C -> X.Y.Z [reason1,reason2]\n'; preserve ordering and return writer errors.

ATOMIC ENGINE. NewEngine validates and starts at revision 1. Plan, Snapshot and Apply are safe for concurrent callers; each Plan corresponds to exactly one revision and owns its result. Snapshot returns deeply owned sorted packages. Restore validates the entire snapshot, requires nonzero Revision, preserves that revision, and owns its inputs. Apply first compares Expected to the current revision (ErrConflict takes precedence over all edit errors). Each edit must contain exactly one nonempty Remove or nonnil Upsert. A package name may occur only once in a batch, including across remove/upsert; removing an absent name is invalid. Upsert replaces the entire package or adds it. Edits are a simultaneous transaction: validate the final candidate graph, allowing joint dependency removal, group upgrades, and forward references within a batch. Reject malformed edits with ErrInvalid, invalid candidate graphs with Build's validation error, and revision overflow with ErrInvalid. Failures return zero Snapshot and leave ALL engine state and future results unchanged. Successful Apply, including an empty batch, increments revision exactly once and replaces graph indexes so later plans use new dependencies/groups; return an owned snapshot. Caller mutation of edits, snapshots and plans must never affect the engine.

ADAPTERS. Wire JSON uses the tags in types.go. jsonapi.ReadPackages/ReadRequest/ReadUpdate/ReadSnapshot reject unknown object fields at any nesting and trailing JSON values or garbage, allow whitespace after one complete value, and propagate reader errors; writers encode the supplied value and propagate writer errors. catalog.Load reads immediate *.json regular entries in filename order, ignores directories/non-json files, decodes one Package per file using normal encoding/json semantics and propagates FS/JSON errors; validation remains Build's responsibility. HTTP Handler must use the same engine and strict JSON decoders: GET /snapshot ->200 snapshot, POST /plan ->200 plan, POST /update ->200 snapshot; decoding/validation errors ->400, revision conflicts ->409; errors have JSON object {"error": nonempty string}; other method/path pairs ->404. Successful/error API responses use application/json. Rejected HTTP requests must not mutate the engine. app.Run accepts exactly ['plan', catalogPath] or ['report', catalogPath], reads a JSON package array from that file and one strict Request from stdin, runs Build/Plan and writes JSON plan or the text report. Return 2 with usage on stderr for argument errors; 1 with nonempty stderr for file/decode/validation/output errors; 0 on success. Do not write stdout before successful planning; CLI main delegates to app.Run. All graph behavior must be shared by direct calls, restored engines, filesystem catalogs, HTTP and CLI. No external dependencies or network services.
